newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco banking sector lifts bourse for second day.
newsitem.headline: Morocco banking sector lifts bourse for second day.

text.p: Morocco's banking sector drove the Casablanca bourse index higher for second consecutive day, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed on Thursday at 430.95, up 0.28 percent on the previous session.

"The banking sector continues to drive the market higher...Blue chips such as Societe Nationale d'Investissement and Eqdom firm also had a positive impact on the bourse activity," a broker at Upline Securities said.
An estimated volume of 59.5 million dirhams was traded on the over the counter market, up from 26.6 million Wednesday.
SNI, one of largest private conglomerates, which has diversified stakes in Morocco's main vital economic sectors including banks, closed at 583 dirhams, up five dirhams on the previous session.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, rose 14 dirhams to close at 690 dirhams.
The bank showed a rise of 5.8 percent in its turnover to 1.289 billion dirhams ($148.1 million) in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, rose one dirhams to close at 310 dirhams.
Eqdom credit company made new gains to trade at 1,102 dirhams, up 32 dirhams compared with Wednesday.
Eqdom plans to increase its capital to 166.6 million ($19.1 million) from 111.1 million dirhams. It said the capital would be increased in two simultanous operations of stock split and rights issue.
Brasseries du Maroc, a leading brewery and a subsidiary of SNI, remained stable at 1,400 dirhams.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate was unchanged at 460 dirhams.
The traded volume on the official market was 23.7 million dirhams, up from 19.02 million in the previous session.
